title: 6.26.2 Check: the Trail game
description: Five multiple-choice questions on the snaking path, passing the turn, min, onMove and the waiting flag. Checked instantly.

questions.question: COLS is 10. Square 13 is in row 1, an odd row, so its column is counted from the right with COLS - 1 - c. Which column is it drawn in?
questions.explanation: 13 % 10 is 3, and on an odd row the column becomes 10 - 1 - 3, which is 6.

questions.question: There are 2 players and turn is 1. What is (turn + 1) % players.length?
questions.explanation: 2 % 2 is 0: after Blue, the turn goes back to Red, at index 0.

questions.question: The finish is square 30. Red is on square 28 and rolls 5. Why does takeTurn move Red with min(p.at + 5, 30)?
options: To make the roll count for less than its full number
To stop Red on square 30, not on square 33 off the board
To send Red back to the start of the whole board
To give the next player a smaller roll on their turn
questions.explanation: min gives the smaller of the two numbers, so a token can never pass the finish.

questions.question: Online, why does the player who rolls send the roll instead of moving their own token?
options: Sending is faster than drawing the token on the screen
The other computer is not able to draw any tokens
Each move, yours too, comes back to both in one order
online.send moves the token on both computers by itself
questions.explanation: Moving tokens only in onMove means both boards run the same list of moves, so they stay the same.

questions.question: Blue lands on a W and the code sets Blue's waiting to true. What happens next?
options: Blue's next turn is skipped once, and the flag goes back to false
Blue moves back 3 squares, and then the turn passes on
Blue keeps on waiting, and never gets another turn
The game ends at once, and Blue is the one who wins it
questions.explanation: nextTurn sees the flag, clears it, and passes the turn once more. Clearing it is what keeps the wait to one turn.
